articles.title: Darius Acuff Jr. Named Kings' Only Untouchable Player in New NBA Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season may just have tipped off, but the Sacramento Kings are already open to trading away nearly anyone on their roster.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season may just have tipped off, but the Sacramento Kings are already open to trading away nearly anyone on their roster.

Kings rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. is the only player the team is unwilling to discuss in trade negotiations, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick .

Acuff Jr. was selected with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after he was named the SEC Player of the Year as a freshman at Arkansas. The 19-year-old has started his professional career on a historic pace, averaging 26.2 points, 7.3 assists and 3.8 rebounds through the first 11 games of his rookie campaign.

The impressive performances from Acuff Jr. has caused "internal excitement" that has the Kings "pondering ways to speed up their roster reconstruction," according to Amick.

Sacramento has plenty of excess weight on its salary cap. Kings center Domantas Sabonis and shooting guard Zach LaVine are both earning over $45 million this season, with Sabonis also accounting for $48.6 million next season, per Spotrac . Forward Keegan Murray is accounting for $24.1 million following the five-year, $140 million extension he signed last year, but he has been hampered by injuries since signing that deal.

The Kings are giving Acuff Jr. plenty of in-game experience early — the rookie is tied for second in field goal attempts per game (22.8) and leads all players with 37.4 minutes per game, per Basketball Reference .

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg Drops Candid Quote About Serving as Warriors' No. 1 Option After Steph Curry Injury
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg has shown tremendous confidence already as a rookie, but he is also self-aware enough to know the pressure that comes with needing to be the No. 1 scoring option for the Golden State Warriors with Stephen Curry injured.
articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg has shown tremendous confidence already as a rookie, but he is also self-aware enough to know the pressure that comes with needing to be the No. 1 scoring option for the Golden State Warriors with Stephen Curry injured.

Speaking to reporters during Friday's shootaround, Lendeborg explained his confidence level is at a "six out of 10" believing he can fulfill Curry's big shoes and the remaining points have him wondering "am I going to be able to live up to it?"

Dray in Support of Yaxel's Trash Talk 🗣️

Curry is expected to miss around one month after the Warriors announced he suffered an oblique abdominal tear. The injury occurred in the first quarter of Golden State's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday.

This will be the first extended absence of the season for Curry. He previously sat out two games on Oct. 24 and Nov. 1 since they were on either end of a back-to-back.

Curry was having one of his best starts to a season in years before the injury. He averaged 30.6 points on 45.7 percent three-point shooting, 4.3 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game in his first nine games.

If there is a reason for Lendeborg to be confident, his numbers in the two games Curry missed suggest he is capable of handling a bigger role. He put up 26 points, nine rebounds and five assists against the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 24.

The Nov. 1 game against the Los Angeles Clippers saw Lendeborg set a career-high with 37 points on 13-of-19 shooting in 34 minutes. He also tied his career-high with six assists in the 124-112 win.

Friday night will be a much tougher test for Lendeborg than those previous two games because the Warriors are facing Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center.

Lendeborg entered the NBA as an older rookie at 24 years old. He has looked ready for every task that has come his way thus far, so there's no reason to think he will be intimidated by this moment.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball sure looks like the difference: Timberwolves and Hornets trending in opposite directions after trade
articles.summary: Minnesota is making moves in the West with LaMelo Ball, while Charlotte is stumbling in the East without him.
articles.body:
We will stipulate that, when it comes to success and struggle in the NBA, the answer is never just one thing. There's plenty that goes into teams' fortunes rising and falling, and all sorts of stuff can factor into the difference between living in the penthouse and taking up residence in the outhouse.

With that caveat in place: While the Minnesota Timberwolves were doing this in Minneapolis on Thursday, en route to dismantling the Dallas Mavericks, 133-94 …

… and the Charlotte Hornets were doing this in Phoenix on the same night, en route to a desultory 101-96 defeat …

… it was hard not to note the Just One Thing that seems to be contributing to the difference between Minnesota and Charlotte. Or, rather, the Guy Wearing No. 1.

After walloping a pretty good Mavs team, the Wolves are 9-3, in third place in the Western Conference, with the NBA's best net rating . They've won five in a row, and six out of eight since losing superstar No. 1 option Anthony Edwards to knee surgery . They've outscored their opponents by a total of 161 points this season; according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes , that's the largest point differential through 12 games in Wolves franchise history — by 50 points .

After falling in Phoenix, mustering just 96 points against the league's fourth-worst defense , the Hornets are now 4-8, tied for 10th in the East, with the NBA's No. 26 net rating . They've lost seven of eight, have logged more turnovers than assists four times in 12 games , and have already failed to crack 100 points six times — as many times as Charlotte finished south of the century mark all of last season .

Again: It's not just that LaMelo Ball used to play for the Hornets, and now he plays for the Wolves. The operating theory for how Charlotte would generate offense in the absence of its one-time linchpin rested largely on continued growth and elevated production from Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and the re-signed Coby White, with a dash of second-unit contribution from veteran Dennis Schröder. The Hornets have gotten a grand total of 97 minutes thus far from White, who's on a minutes restriction as he works his way back from a left calf strain, and Knueppel, who'll miss the next several weeks with a balky left hamstring . Schröder's also on the shelf with a hamstring strain ; Miller, the team's leading scorer, has missed the last two games with a groin injury .

Any team would struggle to score without the bulk of its perimeter firepower, ball-handling and shot creation. It has to be painful, though, to be mired in such a horrific offensive morass mere months after consciously choosing to bid farewell to Ball, the player whom both the eye test and the advanced numbers suggested served as the rising tide that lifted Charlotte's offense last season.

And it must be particularly galling to be suffering through the doldrums while watching LaMelo have exactly the same kind of effusive, elevating effect in the Twin Cities.

Ball had nine of the Wolves' 33 assists in the blowout win over the Mavericks on Thursday — Minnesota's fourth 30-assist game of the season , more than anybody but the Hawks, Warriors, Nuggets and Spurs . Those helpers led to 19 Minnesota points, in addition to the 22 that Ball scored himself; for the season, he's directly creating 56.9 points of offense per 100 possessions for the Wolves, according to Databallr , which is 20th in the NBA — and nearly five points-per-100 more than White, who leads this season's Hornets.

The Wolves generate a higher share of their shots at the rim when LaMelo's on the floor than when he's off it. Their 3-point shooting goes through the roof in his minutes, and nearly every member of the team sees a bump in shot quality when playing alongside him .

The Wolves are more efficient in the half-court when Ball's at the controls, and they get out in transition way more often with him out there. Minnesota's team-wide effective field-goal percentage spikes by 6.5% with LaMelo on the floor — the largest on/off split on the team, and one of the largest among all NBA players to log at least 200 minutes this season, according to Cleaning the Glass .

The numbers tell a compelling story. So, too, does the joy that seems to leap off the screen from so many of the Wolves as they run with LaMelo — orbiting, emulating and ultimately benefiting from the irrepressible style and flow with which he plays.

"I think when you have a guy like Melo, he makes it fun for everybody," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch said after Thursday's win, according to Sarah Todd of the Minnesota Star Tribune . "And the guys can trust in the next pass, next play."

That trust is tougher to come by these days in Charlotte, where the Hornets enter Friday's action ranked dead last in the NBA in points scored per possession , field-goal percentage , free-throw attempts , assists and turnovers , struggling to consistently string together quality possessions, even against lesser defensive outfits.

"How do we stop the bleeding?" White told reporters after a recent loss to the Detroit Pistons. "There's gonna be turnovers. There's gonna be miscommunications on both sides of the ball. How do we not let it continue to derail us from what we're trying to do?"

The loss of a superstar of Edwards' magnitude would've derailed plenty of teams. The Wolves, though, have continued to thrive, buoyed in part by the NBA's No. 1 defense — a unit on which Ball has somewhat surprisingly emerged as a physical and positive contributor at the point of attack. All told, Minnesota has outscored opponents by a whopping 15.5 points per 100 possessions when Ball has played without Edwards — a loftier net rating than even their regular-season leading mark, and more than good enough to stay afloat in the brutally competitive West while Ant continues to rehab his ailing knee.

There are plenty of other factors at play. The Hornets have underperformed their expected shot quality by more than any other team in the NBA thus far, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking; the combination of some regression to the mean and the hopefully healthy return of some key pieces should help bolster their offense. And there's plenty of credit to go around in Minnesota, from Rudy Gobert's perpetually stalwart work on the back line to Finch getting career-best play from the likes of Jonathan Kuminga, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland to a collective closing kick that has the Wolves ranked second in the NBA in fourth-quarter net rating .

"We've definitely [elevated] our play in the fourth quarters on both sides of the ball," Finch said . "Getting key stops, rebounding really well, executing, finding really good shots. And LaMelo's been at the heart of a lot of that on offense."

LaMelo's presence has been at the heart of a lot of what's gone well for the Wolves, and his absence, it seems, has been at the heart of a lot of what's haunting the Hornets. It's never just one thing. Sometimes, though, one thing can make one hell of a big difference.

articles.title: Dejounte Murray Trade Idea After New Orleans Pelicans Guard Requests Out
articles.summary: Dejounte Murray wants to be traded from the New Orleans Pelicans, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. This aligns with earlier reporting from Shamit Dua of In The N.O. that both player and team believed it was time to go their separate ways.
articles.body:
Dejounte Murray wants to be traded from the New Orleans Pelicans, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . This aligns with earlier reporting from Shamit Dua of In The N.O. that both player and team believed it was time to go their separate ways.

Now, the divorce process will accelerate.

As it just so happens, people inside the Phoenix Suns' locker room were reportedly annoyed that they don't have a real point guard on the roster . The team has already registered interest in Murray, per Chris Haynes of NBA TV .

Not sure about you, but it sounds like there's a deal to be made here.

In: Jalen Green, 2027 second-round pick, $3.5 million cash

As In The N.O.'s Shamit Dua writes, "many around the league believe the Pelicans and Murray would like to work together to find a better situation for the veteran guard." We can quibble over whether the Suns count as a "better situation." But landing on a team obsessed with playing past Apr. 11 makes at least slightly more sense.

Though Green isn't the cleanest fit in The Big Easy, he's nearly six years younger and more athletic than Murray. He also doesn't have an Achilles injury in his rearview. Last season was the first time he racked up a significant number of absences.

Despite identical career clips from beyond the arc, Green is the more dangerous shooter of the two. He moves differently when stationed away from the ball and ranked in the 64th percentile or higher of pull-up three-point efficiency during each of his first three seasons, according to BBall Index . Murray has cleared the latter threshold just once.

The Pelicans are burning most of their space beneath the luxury tax by taking on an additional $3.5 million salary. They'll get it back in the inevitable Jordan Poole buyout. Phoenix is also sending New Orleans the requisite cash to make up the difference. Extra seconds are always useful, too.

Most importantly, the Pelicans are opening additional runway for sophomore Jeremiah Fears. Few consider him lead-guard material, but head of basketball operations Joe Dumars is "extremely high" on him, according to Dua. New Orleans can now hand him the reins unchecked while also carving out extra on-ball usage for Zion Williamson and Derik Queen.

Out: Jalen Green, 2027 second-round pick, $3.5 million cash

Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports that " there's some growing frustration " in the Suns' locker room because the "roster does not have a point guard that could organize" the offense. If only Phoenix had a 2033 first-round pick to dangle in higher-end deals.

Murray isn't the perfect solution. His three-point efficiency has cratered since leaving Atlanta, and he's attempting his fewest triples per 36 minutes since he was a member of the San Antonio Spurs. That gets dicey for a Suns offense already light on shooting.

Capable ball-handling takes precedence anyway. Phoenix is too reliant on Devin Booker and Dillon Brooks for make-something-out-of-nothing plays. Collin Gillespie would already be starting if the Suns knew what they were doing, but he's not the spiffiest passer and gets targeted constantly on defense.

Acquiring Murray adds another layer of playmaking to the offensive ranks. He has routinely averaged more rim assists per 75 possessions than any ball-handler currently on the roster and has crafty enough live-dribble vision to optimize touches for Khaman Maluach. He remains a defensive upgrade over Green, too.

The Suns can balk at including the second-rounder and $3.5 million. Green is younger. But he's a wild card and a below-average passer. Murray has the higher baseline and could cost Phoenix noticeably less if his unlikely incentives don't cash.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Warriors' Draymond Green Says Rockets 'Do Some Bulls--t,' Addresses Claim They're a 'Dirty' Team
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green doesn't believe that the Houston Rockets are a dirty team despite a recent on-court altercation between the two squads.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green doesn't believe that the Houston Rockets are a dirty team despite a recent on-court altercation between the two squads.

"I don't get off into the dirty thing," Green said on Friday's episode of The Draymond Green Show (h/t HoopsHype ). "Every now and then you see some people that just do things that are down right dirty. And it happens and when it does, I'll speak on it. Do they do some bulls--t when we play them? Absolutely. I think the thing is that may irritate me the most is like they play super physical but then they start flopping sometimes, you know? So, I would say like that irritates me more, but I'm not going to sit here and call them dirty team."

During Houston's 115-108 win over Golden State on Wednesday, Rockets guard Marcus Smart was ejected after throwing a punch at Warriors center Charles Bassey.

Bassey called Smart's actions "dirty" after the game.

"He's been playing dirty the whole game, man," Bassey said, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area. "I remember in the first half, I was trying to set a screen. Bro, he grabbed my knees. He was playing dirty."

Smart eventually received a three-game suspension from the NBA.

Houston has recorded 52 wins in each of the past two seasons largely due to its hard-nosed defense, ranking No. 6 in the league with a 112.1 defensive rating during its 2025-26 campaign (via NBA.com ).

This year, the Rockets' 109.3 defensive rating represents the seventh-best mark among all teams.

Green has similarly developed a reputation for his aggressive defensive approach that occasionally includes extracurricular activities, earning nine All-Defensive Team selections and one Defensive Player of the Year award during his tenure in Golden State.

He's also been ejected from 23 regular-season games throughout his career, the second-most in NBA history (h/t Mack Baltes of Warriors Wire).

The next meeting between the Rockets and Warriors will take place on Dec. 30.

articles.title: Un memorable Robinson lidera la épica remontada del Barça en el OAKA
articles.standfirst: Los culés iban 14 abajo, pero el base hizo 16 puntos en los últimos cinco minutos incluidos los 13 finales de su equipo y el triple ganador para tumbar al líder Panathinaikos
articles.summary: Los culés iban 14 abajo, pero el base hizo 16 puntos en los últimos cinco minutos incluidos los 13 finales de su equipo y el triple ganador para tumbar al líder Panathinaikos
articles.body: Un memorable sprint final de Justin Robinson le dio al Barcelona una heroica victoria en el OAKA ante el líder Panathinaikos (74-76). Ahora mismo, no hay un jugador más determinante en Europa en los instantes decisivos. Nadie como él para darle los balones calientes. Los azulgranas arrancaron el último cuarto 14 abajo (57-43), pero entre Tyrese Martin, con 12 puntos casi seguidos, y el base, que hizo 16 con cuatro triples en los últimos cinco minutos incluido el ganador a falta de cuatro segundos, obraron una remontada que congeló el pabellón ateniense. Quinto triunfo consecutivo para un conjunto culé que ha vuelto a demostrar que es irreductible. Porque se plantó en Atenas con cuatro bajas (Punter, Makoundou, Núñez y Evbuomwan), porque hasta el último cuarto tuvo una noche nefasta en el tiro, porque en el tercer cuarto estuvo cerca del naufragio, porque sufrió un arbitraje sibilino... Pero un día más se agarró al parqué y consiguió salir con vida. Cuando el Barça formaba su plantilla en verano, además de desconocidos para el gran público, estaba fichando a guerreros que nunca bajan los brazos. Minuto a minuto, fue resistiendo el Barça. Al final del primer cuarto, 17-17 tras un mal inicio. Al descanso, 33-32 después de verse siete abajo (31-24) y levantarse con dos triples de Parra y Robinson. Llevaban los culés 4/16 desde el arco. Ritmo lento. Poco acierto. Problemas de faltas de Parra y Brizuela, referente en los últimos partidos. Se echaba de menos a Punter y en el Panathinaikos aparecía ya Nunn (10 puntos y acabaría con 19). En el tercer cuarto, el Barça zozobró. Recibió un 7-0 para arrancar y la inspiración de Francisco (17), con dos triples, y los tiros libres estiraron la renta hasta una máxima de 57-43. Los culés metieron tres canastas en juego en ese periodo y perdieron seis balones. Cada ataque era una tortura ante la crecida física del Panathinaikos. Parcial de 24-11. ¿Remontar un partido así en el OAKA? Parecía imposible. No para este equipo. Martin, negado hasta entonces, encendió la mecha con nueve puntos casi seguidos. Luego añadiría un triple más para acercarse a 66-63. Sólo dos entradas de Nunn evitaban el colapso total de los locales, que no metían una de fuera. Un tapón colosal de Nebo a Yabusele echó más gasolina al fuego azulgrana. El partido estaba donde le gustan a Robinson. Con hielo en la sangre el base puso el empate a 66 y con dos tiros libres consumó la remontada. Respondió Francisco con un triple y replicó de nuevo el base azulgrana con otro. Hayes-Davis, que no había anotado en juego, desequilibró para el Panathinaikos con cinco puntos seguidos: 74-73 a falta de 19 segundos. La última tenía que ser para Robinson. ¿Quién sino él? A falta de cuatro segundos, se jugó un triple frontal ante la defensa de Bonga y el balón tocó la parte posterior del aro. En lugar de salir rebotado, cayó suavemente en la canasta. Era el punto 33 del Barça en el último cuarto, uno más de los que metió al descanso. Robinson metió los últimos 13 de este equipo tocado físicamente pero que jamás se rinde. Ni en el OAKA ni ante la pasarela de estrellas de Obradovic. 74 - Panathinaikos (17+16+24+17): Francisco (17), Badio (-), Bonga (4), Hernangómez (8), Mitoglou (2) -cinco inicial-, Sloukas (1), Hayes Davis (9), Grant (3), Nunn (19), Lessort (5) y Yabusele (6) 76 - Barça (17+15+11+33): Robinson (24), Umude (9), Martin (13), Parra (5), Nebo (5) -cinco inicial-, Gibson (-), Brizuela (4), Nkamhoua (7), Balcerowski (7) y Minaya (2), Árbitros: Mehdi Difallah, Damir Javor y Milivoje Jovcic. Eliminados: Parra (min.37) Incidencias: partido de la undécima jornada de la Euroliga disputado en el Telekom Center de Atenas.

articles.title: Zion Williamson's Trade Value Assessed by NBA Exec in Honest Quote Amid Pelicans' Struggles
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans may have to give up on getting back a significant return for Zion Williamson should the franchise decide to dismantle the roster after Dejounte Murray's reported trade request.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans may have to give up on getting back a significant return for Zion Williamson should the franchise decide to dismantle the roster after Dejounte Murray's reported trade request .

"I was texting with an executive, asking about a potential Zion market," ESPN's Tim MacMahon said Friday on NBA Today (4:10 mark of the video below).

"He says, 'Can you trade Zion? Sure. Can you get a big return for him? No way.'"

Williamson has gotten off to an efficient start to the season so far, shooting 62.2 percent from the field while averaging 21.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and two steals while appearing in 11 of the Pelicans' last 12 games.

He called out his team by saying players and coaches needed to "look in the mirror" after conceding a blowout Wednesday loss to the visiting Brooklyn Nets.

Injury and conditioning issues have impacted Williamson throughout his eight-year career with the Pelicans, although last season he averaged 21 points while playing in 62 games. Pelicans head of basketball operations Joe Dumars said in September he considered Williamson to be "in impeccable condition."

Williamson met games played criteria to make his $42.2 million cap hit for this season fully guaranteed, per Spotrac . He has not yet guaranteed the $44.9 million 2027-28 cap hit remaining on his deal before he is scheduled to hit unrestricted free agency ahead of his age-28 season.

The Pelicans could potentially already have at least one landing spot to consider for Murray, who has been ruled out of Friday's NBA Cup action with a left ankle sprain.

NBA insider Chris Haynes reported the Phoenix Suns had "registered interest" in Murray shortly after The Athletic's Sam Amick reported the franchise is "motivated to swap [Jalen Green] for a proven point guard."

Charania had reported earlier on NBA Today the Pelicans and Murray's agent Rich Paul had been working "for the last several days" to resolve Murray's trade request.

It sounds like Murray is more likely to be immediately on the move than Williamson as the Pelicans look to regroup from a 4-8 start that has left the team sitting 12th in the Western Conference.

articles.title: Pelicans evaluating possibilities after trade request from Dejounte Murray, who recently rebutted criticism on social media
articles.summary: Murray is currently in his third season with the team.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans are evaluating potential trade opportunities for Dejounte Murray after a trade request from the All-Star guard, the team announced Friday .

The news comes the same week the 30-year-old Murray rebutted criticism on social media with since-deleted posts, one of which reportedly featured profanity. The Pelicans are 4-8 this season, including 1-8 in the games Murray has appeared in.

Murray won't play in Friday night's NBA Cup group-play game between New Orleans and the Memphis Grizzlies, the Pelicans announced, citing his left ankle sprain . His agent Rich Paul and Pelicans officials were reported by ESPN's Shams Charania to be working on a resolution earlier in the day.

The Phoenix Suns have expressed interest in the 2022 All-Star, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes.

The 2026-27 campaign is his third with the Pelicans, with whom he's currently averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.6 steals per game.

That said, Murray is shooting just 29.6% from 3, and he's committed four turnovers twice so far.

In the fallout of a 145-111 home loss to the 3-8 Brooklyn Nets, the X account for Pro Pels Talk, a Pelicans podcast, posted an array of game clips, breaking down the game film without mincing words. The commentary that accompanied some of those clips questioned Murray's on-court effort .

As reported by The Athletic , Murray responded to one of those posts, which showcased footage of him apparently misplacing a pass intended for forward Saddiq Bey. The ball ended up low and away, resulting in a turnover, whereas Bey seemed to be asking for it near chest level.

"Ohhhhh let's talk about it," Murray wrote back on X in a since-deleted post, per The Athletic. "When you run post plays, are they suppose to catch on the block or the 3pt line? Let's hear it Mr social media coach, Gm and President? You have no f***ing clue what we dealing with.

"Maybe you should ask the whole team individually how they feel on a serious note and then … rethink alot of s***."

Before that, Murray engaged with an NBACentral X post that noted how the Pelicans are 3-0 without him this season.

In a quote post, Murray used a slew of crying laughing emojis and then said this, as captured in a screenshot by a social media user :

"From what's going on INSIDE This sounds like someone hit you to say this!! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!!!!!!"

On Friday, he apparently reposted Charania's report about him wanting out of New Orleans. That repost no longer appears on his X feed, however.

Charania went on "NBA Today" Friday after breaking the news to flesh it out more:

"In the last several days, I'm told, Murray has met with the organization, has made it clear to them that he wants to go somewhere else and play a meaningful, key role on another team," Charania said on the program . "And we've seen Dejounte Murray, especially on social media, express his frustration with how things are going there. Clearly, it is not working out there. He is not going to be playing basketball in New Orleans for the time moving forward here."

"In the last several days, I'm told, Murray has met with the organization, has made it clear to them that he wants to go somewhere else and play a meaningful, key role on another team," Charania said on the program .

"And we've seen Dejounte Murray, especially on social media, express his frustration with how things are going there. Clearly, it is not working out there. He is not going to be playing basketball in New Orleans for the time moving forward here."

Charania noted that in Murray's absence, the Pelicans will turn over the lead guard position to 2025 No. 7 overall pick Jeremiah Fears. The 20-year-old Oklahoma product has averaged 18 points and nine assists in the three games Murray has missed this season.

Murray's been available for only 54 Pelicans games since he came aboard ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. He suffered a torn Achilles that season , and that injury kept him out of a good portion of last season, too .

Murray's best NBA season occurred in 2021-22, when he earned his All-Star recognition and led the league in steals during his final go-around with the San Antonio Spurs. He also spent two seasons with the Atlanta Hawks. They ultimately traded him to the Pelicans for two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr., E.J. Liddell and Cody Zeller.

articles.title: 'Physical as F--k,' JJ Redick Outlines Lakers' Identities After 'Audit' of 11-2 Start to NBA Season
articles.summary: JJ Redick says his coaching and analytics staff put together a 21-page "audit" detailing statistics that back up what he sees as the Los Angeles Lakers' identity after an 11-2 start to the season.
articles.body:
JJ Redick says his coaching and analytics staff put together a 21-page "audit" detailing statistics that back up what he sees as the Los Angeles Lakers' identity after an 11-2 start to the season.

Redick went over the audit with his team ahead of Sunday's game at the Phoenix Suns, he told reporters Friday (h/t ESPN's Dave McMenamin).

"We filtered through our offensive stuff based on our identities of who we want to be offensively: Organized, unselfish, advantage-based," Redick said. "And then we went to our defense, and our three identities: Organized, physical as f--k, and relentless."

Redick concluded, "We've done that for the last two and a half seasons. Everything that we present to the team lines up with who we're trying to be."

The Lakers are in the middle of a three-day break since their last game, a Wednesday victory at the Milwaukee Bucks that marked the team's seventh win in a row.

After taking on the 5-6 Suns this Sunday in Phoenix, the Lakers are scheduled for a four-game homestand against struggling teams in the 4-8 Charlotte Hornets and the one-win Utah Jazz and Sacramento Kings.

Redick will look to take advantage of that home stretch to further solidify his team's identity before the Lakers match up against the San Antonio Spurs later this month in what could be a battle for the top spot in the West.

articles.title: Montrezl Harrell Reveals He Nearly Fought Paul George During 2020 NBA Bubble, 'I Will Beat Your Ass'
articles.summary: Former NBA center Montrezl Harrell explained why he was almost involved in a fight with Los Angeles Clippers teammate Paul George during a second-round playoff clash with the Denver Nuggets in the 2020 NBA bubble.
articles.body:
Former NBA center Montrezl Harrell explained why he was almost involved in a fight with Los Angeles Clippers teammate Paul George during a second-round playoff clash with the Denver Nuggets in the 2020 NBA bubble.

During a Friday appearance on the Kowch Potatoes podcast, Harrell revealed that the disagreement stemmed from a miscommunication on defense while guarding Nuggets star Nikola Jokić.

"Bruh tried to start talking to me crazy and then tried to address me like, 'Bro, who you talking to?' Once he said that, all the basketball went out the window," Harrell said (0:57 mark). "I didn't think about nothing else. Lou had to grab me, Pat came up and grabbed me."

"I said, 'Bro, I will beat your ass. F--k all the basketball s--t, I will knock you the f--k out bruh. I'm not even playing with you.' I just started letting him have it," he added.

The high tensions between Harrell and George don't come as a complete shock, as reports from the bubble in Sept. 2020 indicated that the two players didn't see eye-to-eye.

Still, the Clippers were viewed as a top contender to capture a championship at the time with a rotation that featured George, Harrell, Kawhi Leonard, Lou Williams and Patrick Beverley.

Los Angeles compiled a 44-20 record to start its 2019-20 campaign before the NBA moved to the bubble in Orlando amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Clippers took down the Dallas Mavericks in the first round of the playoffs that year, but ended up blowing a 3-1 series lead over the Nuggets in the second round before they were eliminated.

George struggled against Denver, shooting just 38.2 percent from the field and 33.3 percent from behind the arc across the final three games of the series.

Harrell averaged 11.7 points and 2.6 rebounds per game while connecting on 54.9 percent of his field goals in the second round.

He ultimately joined the Los Angeles Lakers during the ensuing offseason, while George remained with the Clippers for four more years before signing with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2024.

articles.title: Josh Hart and wife Shannon bought a Florida mansion for $4.75 million in 2022; four years later, the Knicks star relisted it for $5.69 million after an unsuccessful earlier sale attempt
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Josh Hart is trying to sell his Florida mansion again, putting the property on the market for $5.69 million after an earlier attempt
articles.body: New York Knicks star Josh Hart is trying to sell his Florida mansion again, putting the property on the market for $5.69 million after an earlier attempt failed. Hart and his wife, Shannon Hart, bought the five-bedroom home in Pinecrest, Florida, for $4.75 million in 2022. The couple first listed it for $5.9 million last year before lowering the asking price to $5.8 million and eventually taking it off the market. Now, the 31-year-old basketball player is making another attempt to sell the property, which offers a pool, a private putting green and several outdoor living spaces.Why has Josh Hart put his Florida mansion up for sale again?The latest asking price is $5.69 million, slightly below the amount the couple wanted when they first tried to sell the house. The property is being marketed by Michael Martinez of ONE Sotheby’s International Realty. The Wall Street Journal first reported the relisting.Hart and Shannon bought the house in November 2022 for $4.75 million. Their decision to sell comes after they spent less time in Florida, as Hart’s basketball career and family life have kept them mostly in New York.The couple initially put the mansion up for sale in 2025, asking $5.995 million. They later lowered the price to $5.85 million but did not find a buyer. The property was eventually taken off the market during the summer of 2026.Now, they are giving the house another chance to find a buyer. The current asking price is still higher than what they paid for it in 2022, although the final sale price will depend on whether a buyer agrees to the terms.What does Josh Hart’s $5.69 million Florida mansion look like?The house is in Coconut Palm Estates, a residential community in Pinecrest, Florida. It has five bedrooms, five bathrooms and approximately 5,800 square feet of living space. The property sits on a quiet cul-de-sac, offering the family more privacy.The listing describes the house as:“Tucked away on a peaceful cul-de-sac in Pinecrest’s coveted Coconut Palm Estates, this exceptional 5-bedroom, 5-bath residence offers the perfect balance of privacy, sophistication, and resort-inspired living,”The home has high ceilings and large windows that allow plenty of natural light into its rooms. Its open layout connects the main living and dining areas, giving the family plenty of space to spend time together or welcome guests.The kitchen is one of the main features of the property. It has wooden cabinets, a large white island, modern appliances and a walk-in pantry. There is also a breakfast nook where the family can sit together for meals or spend a quiet morning.The listing gives a closer look at the layout:“Thoughtfully designed with an expansive open floor plan, the home showcases spacious living and entertaining areas, a charming breakfast nook, a beautifully appointed kitchen with designer appliances and walk-in pantry, and the convenience of second-floor laundry facilities,”The main bedroom also has its own balcony overlooking the property’s green surroundings. The bathroom features a freestanding bathtub and a double-sink vanity, while the walk-in closet has built-in storage and a central island.Outside, the property has several spaces designed for spending time with family and friends. There is a swimming pool, covered terraces, an outdoor summer kitchen and a private putting green. Hart also installed an outdoor sound system, adding another feature to the backyard.The property listing highlights these outdoor features:“Designed for seamless indoor-outdoor living, expansive covered terraces provide inviting spaces for relaxation and entertaining, while a resort-style pool, summer kitchen, and private putting green create the ultimate setting for alfresco dining and year-round enjoyment,”It also describes the house as a “remarkable opportunity to experience refined South Florida living in one of Pinecrest’s most desirable neighborhoods.”Why is Josh Hart spending less time at his Florida home?Although the Florida property was a place where Hart could relax during the basketball offseason, he now spends most of his time in New York. His professional commitments with the Knicks have also made regular trips to South Florida less convenient.Speaking to The Wall Street Journal, Hart explained that the family still has good memories of the area and has not ruled out returning in the future.“We will be back. We loved the location,” he told the Journal, revealing that he would be buying another home in the area after he retires.Hart also spoke about the part of the house he enjoyed the most. While the mansion has several expensive features, including its swimming pool and private putting green, his favourite place was a much simpler part of the home.“The ability to go down there, make coffee, hang out with the boys, watch a little TV, kick it by the breakfast nook—that was the highlight.”His comments suggest that the property was more than just a place to stay during the offseason. It gave him and his family a comfortable space to spend time together away from his basketball commitments.However, with the family now spending more time in New York, the Florida house is back on the market.Did Josh Hart and Shannon Hart buy another home in New York?The Florida mansion is not the only property the couple have purchased in recent years. In 2024, Josh and Shannon bought a home in New York for an undisclosed amount.The property was purchased from local Compass real estate agent Kim Arenas. Details about its exact location, size and features have not been made public.Arenas shared her experience of working with the couple and helping them find their new home. She also spoke about the work that went into the process, from looking at properties that were not publicly listed to completing the final details.In a social media post, Arenas wrote:“We are thrilled to have had the opportunity to help these amazing clients find their home! From searching off-market homes, exploring the plans to adding the final touches, it was a wonderful journey building their new home.“We can’t wait for their family to create lasting memories here. And of course, go Knicks!”The purchase also helps explain why the couple may be spending less time at their Florida property. With a home in New York and Hart’s professional commitments with the Knicks, the family has another place to spend time throughout the year.For now, the Pinecrest mansion is available for $5.69 million, and the couple are hoping their second attempt to sell it will bring a buyer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Stephen Curry's defense of Ayesha gets Stephen A. Smith's heartfelt praise following kissing scene debate
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith has praised Stephen Curry for his response to criticism aimed at Ayesha Curry.
articles.body: Stephen A. Smith has praised Stephen Curry for his response to criticism aimed at Ayesha Curry. Gilbert Arenas and Emmanuel Acho had both brought up a clip from her Roku project, Second Chance Holiday, in which she kisses a male actor, and criticized her over it. Curry answered with a pointed but polite statement, and Arenas, Acho and Nick Young have all apologized since. Smith took the topic to his own show to speak about Curry’s character, not the clip. The Warriors superstar is also missing time with an oblique tear.What did Stephen Curry say about the criticism of Ayesha?Curry’s message was polite and pointed. Anytime Ayesha shows up in a headline, the Warriors guard suggested, people should offer “the happy hands, the congratulations” and make any apology as loud as the coverage was. Curry then thanked everyone for the free promotion and pointed viewers to Second Chance Holiday on Roku, where Ayesha stars.Smith zeroed in on the tone. Even when Curry is calling people out, he said, the guard stays nice about it. Arenas, Young and Acho got credit for apologizing. The reason for bringing it up at all, Smith explained, was to shine a light on Curry. Smith’s verdict: “Just one of the most decent brothers you’ll ever meet in your life.”Smith also said anyone with something negative to say about a person close to Curry should stop and think first.Smith wants the Warriors to lean on Yaxel Lendeborg without CurryThe praise arrives while Golden State adjusts to life without its star. An MRI confirmed an oblique tear for Curry, and Smith has a view on who should pick up the slack. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is his answer. Smith said he loves the kid and is a big fan of what Lendeborg brings.Smith was careful about expectations. “Nobody is Steph Curry,” he said. Still, he thinks the rookie can be given the ball more often and lead a more active offense for the team.Draymond Green is part of the same plan. Smith wants Green to be more efficient and aggressive on offense, though not to an extreme. Three points a game is too low, Smith agreed. Ten or 11 is about Green’s range, and if Green is also playmaking and defending, that works for Smith. ESPN’s Kendrick Perkins argues Green is the player who has to step up.Golden State is 8-4 and sixth in the West, ahead of Oklahoma City and Memphis and behind Portland and Houston. articles.summary: Dejounte Murray's representatives at Klutch Sports requested a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, who say they will evaluate opportunities.
articles.body: The apparently strained relationship between Dejounte Murray and the New Orleans Pelicans took another turn Friday. Representatives for the All-Star guard at Klutch Sports requested a trade, prompting the team to say it would evaluate potential opportunities. "Today, Dejounte Murray’s representatives informed us of his request to be traded," the Pelicans said in a statement. "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization." Murray, 30, was ruled out Friday night against the Memphis Grizzlies due to a left ankle sprain. Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley said Murray was not at Smoothie King Center. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "He’s not in the building, from what I’ve been told," Mosley said. The Pelicans acquired Murray in a June 2024 trade with the Atlanta Hawks in exchange for two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr. and E.J. Liddell. David Griffin, then serving as the Pelicans’ executive vice president of basketball operations, viewed Murray as a defender and playmaker who could provide ball-handling help for Zion Williamson, but he never approached the play that had earned him All-Star honors in 2022. DEJOUNTE MURRAY ACCUSES NEW ORLEANS PELICANS OF INSIDE 'SABOTAGE' IN DELETED SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS Murray’s tenure with the Pelicans was dogged by injuries. He broke his hand in the 2024 season opener and then suffered a season-ending Achilles injury in January 2025. Over the last three seasons, Murray has played just 54 games with New Orleans, averaging 16.6 points, 6.6 assists and 5.9 rebounds. The Pelicans have gone 1-8 with him in the lineup. Murray's salary is reportedly $32.8 million this season. He has a player option for $30.8 million next season. He recently made his frustrations with the team clear through several critical social media posts. After one social media reporter mentioned the Pelicans were 3-0 without him in the lineup, Murray wrote back: "From what’s going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! THE ‘SABOTAGE’ IS REAL!" The tweet was deleted shortly after. The timing of Murray’s trade request drew some scrutiny, as it surfaced while the Pelicans were on a four-game losing streak. Nevertheless, Mosley said his focus remained on the players available to him and maintaining the team’s standards. "How well we play is very important to me, and making sure that we keep up that standard," Mosley said. "That’s why it’s so glaring when we don’t, because I know what this team has shown during training camp, what it has shown during the preseason." "The first couple games didn’t go on the win column, but the way we played, we did a lot of good things. … As the leader of this group, how we’ve been playing these last three games have not been a representation of this organization, the city, of the way we said we were going to play. articles.title: Yaxel Talks Steph Curry, NBA All-Star Goals and More in New Video Amid Rookie Season with Warriors
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg says his goal for his rookie season with the Golden State Warriors is to earn an All-Star nod while helping spark another dominant season from Stephen Curry.
articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg says his goal for his rookie season with the Golden State Warriors is to earn an All-Star nod while helping spark another dominant season from Stephen Curry.

"Steph, he's old, he's grandpa-aged," Lendeborg joked in an interview with Taylor Rooks aired Friday on NBA on Prime. "So, I try my best to not let those last years go to waste, like everybody's saying. I want the best for him, because he's done so much for the Warriors, and I feel like I owe a lot to the Warriors."

Lendeborg continued, "I want to be somebody who brought life back into him. I want to be the guy that shifts that mindset, actually gives the Warriors a better shot than they've had the last couple of years. Just the spark plug, the young guy who comes in and changes the whole persona of the team."

Dray in Support of Yaxel's Trash Talk 🗣️

Lendeborg is the only member of the Warriors who has started every game of the team's 8-4 run to open the season. He ranks second only to Curry for the team scoring lead with 21.7 points per game and has been regularly tasked with defensive matchups ranging from Victor Wembanyama to Kevin Durant.

The 24-year-old told Rooks he was expecting to serve as more of role player when the Warriors first selected him out of Michigan with the No. 11 pick out of the 2026 draft.

"When I first got drafted, I just expected to be a guy that sits in the corner, waits for a shot. Maybe I'm just, like, seven points a game," Lendeborg said. "Now I somewhat became the second option on offense, and that's definitely something I never thought would happen in the NBA."

Lendeborg is now an early favorite for the 2027 Rookie of the Year award, although he told Rooks he felt detractors would criticize him whether he won or loss because of his age.

"The award would be nice, but I'm trying to be an All-Star this year," Lendeborg told Rooks.

The Warriors are ranked sixth in the Western Conference heading into a Friday night NBA Cup matchup against Wembanyama and the Spurs. Lendeborg will look to continue making his case for an All-Star bid while helping keep his new team in playoff contention as Stephen Curry recovers from an oblique abdominal tear ESPN's Shams Charania reported could sideline the Warriors star for around a month.

articles.title: No. 24 Kentucky escapes Northern Arizona's upset bid on Alex Wilkins' 3-pointer with 2 seconds left
articles.summary: The Wildcats were nearly upset by the 0-3 Lumberjacks after suffering a blowout loss to Kansas on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Alex Wilkins drilled a 3-pointer from the right elbow of the arc with 2.2 seconds left in the game to help No. 24 Kentucky escape an upset with a 78-77 win over Northern Arizona at Rupp Arena on Friday night.

Northern Arizona came into Lexington with an 0-3 record and were 35.5-point underdogs. Yet the Lumberjacks were 22 seconds away from a shocking win. Cade Bennett sank what appeared to be the dagger 3-pointer from the top of the arc, putting the fans at Rupp Arena in shock.

Wildcats head coach Mark Pope was facing the worst loss of his career following an 89-69 loss to No. 15 Kansas at Chicago's United Center on Tuesday. But Mason Williams hit a jumper from just inside the 3-point line to pull the Wildcats to within two points.

Max Majerle and Chris Komin then each missed free throws at the front end of 1-and-1 fouls for Northern Arizona, giving Kentucky an opportunity to tie the score or take the lead with eight seconds remaining.

The Wildcats did not call a timeout after Komin's miss. Ousmane N'Diaye snared the rebound and passed to Williams, who fired the ball up the court to Wilkins. The sophomore took three dribbles, the third with a jab step that backed Bennett off him to get an open 3. =

Midway through the first half, Northern Arizona stayed close with Kentucky before the Wildcats went on an 11-3 run to take a double-digit lead. Komin then hit consecutive 3-pointers to follow up two straight 3s by Kentucky's Milan Momcilovic. One more 3 from Komin pulled the Lumberjacks to within six points before a Malachi Moreno layup put the Wildcats ahead 45-37 at halftime.

Northern Arizona began the second half with a 14-2 run to take a one-point advantage. A 3 from Wilkins briefly put Kentucky back ahead before the Lumberjacks again regained the lead and kept the Wildcats behind for the next seven minutes. There were six lead changes over the ensuing four minutes until Bennett hit what appeared to be the game-winner.

"I hope everybody at Rupp had fun. It was a pretty exciting game," Pope said. "It's pretty entertaining, if not well-executed. " "I think it's going to be a fun team to follow," he added. "This team is, they're with one exception, they're finding ways to win games and we will continue down that path as we try and kind of settle the ship and execute better."

"I hope everybody at Rupp had fun. It was a pretty exciting game," Pope said. "It's pretty entertaining, if not well-executed. "

"I think it's going to be a fun team to follow," he added. "This team is, they're with one exception, they're finding ways to win games and we will continue down that path as we try and kind of settle the ship and execute better."

Komin scored 25 points, shooting 5-for-8 on 3-pointers, with 7 rebounds and 6 steals for the Lumberjacks. Freshman forward Lucas Toukam added 18 points with 6 boards, while Bennett and Ryan Abelman each scored 9.

Wilkins was one of three Wildcats with 14 points, joining Moreno and Momcilovic. N'Diaye added 11 points with six rebounds.

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry confronts critic over controversial motherhood remarks as Stephen Curry’s family finds itself back in the spotlight
articles.summary: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry replied to an online critic on Friday after an old podcast clip of hers went viral.
articles.body: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry replied to an online critic on Friday after an old podcast clip of hers went viral. The video, reposted Wednesday night, features her saying she once did not want kids or marriage. One X user called her comments disturbing and accused her of complaining about motherhood. Ayesha answered with a short, direct post. She says she was only answering a question about her childhood plans. The exchange comes days after the Warriors superstar defended her over a Roku movie role and remarks from former NBA players.Why did Ayesha Curry respond to a critic over her motherhood remarks?The clip comes from Ayesha’s 2025 appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast. She described herself back then as a career-focused woman who did not want kids, did not want to marry and never dreamed about wearing a wedding dress. Stephen Curry’s wife was describing her younger self, not her feelings about parenting now.When the video resurfaced, an X user wrote a long reply. The post called her remarks disturbing and said a husband, children and the chance to be present while raising them are blessings many women pray for. It also said motherhood takes sacrifice, but children are not why anyone misses out on life."Watching Ayesha Curry complain about motherhood is disturbing. Having a husband, beautiful children and the opportunity to be present while raising them are blessings so many women pray for," the user commented on the post.The user further added to the controversy, “Motherhood requires sacrifice. We all know that. But your children are not the reason you missed out on life… Imagine being so focused on what you think motherhood took from you that you fail to appreciate everything God has given you… And here you are complaining about the very blessings they are begging God for.”Ayesha saw it Friday morning and answered. “I’ve never complained a day in my life,” she wrote. She said the question she had been asked was about what she pictured for herself as a little girl. Her point was simple. A comment about an old mindset had been read as a present-day complaint. She did not argue about parenting or defend her choices. She corrected the framing and left it there.Curry’s Instagram message to Arenas and YoungHer role in the Roku rom-com Second Chance Holiday set off the earlier round of talk. Gilbert Arenas called Ayesha “the only blemish” on an otherwise spotless family image and compared her with other NBA stars’ wives. Nick Young also weighed in.Curry answered on Wednesday in an Instagram message that named Nick Young, Arenas and Emmanuel. He said they were offering opinions on something they did not know about, and that it spoke to a bigger conversation about how women are viewed and what they are allowed to do. He cited ignorance about how acting works. The Warriors superstar first tried to laugh it off, he said, but “something needs to be said.”He asked them to offer congratulations on the movie, and said any apology should be as loud as the shows that led with the topic. He ended by thanking the podcasters for promoting the film and urging them to show his wife more respect.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Eyes New Contract After Admitting Frustration With Her Game Ahead Of Major 2027 Transformation
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham says she is not satisfied with her game and plans to spend the offseason changing it.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham says she is not satisfied with her game and plans to spend the offseason changing it. The 30-year-old Fever guard said so on No Hesitation, the podcast she co-hosts with Drew Hanlen. Free agency opens January 30. Cunningham’s one-year deal is about to run out, and Indiana is bringing in a new front office after an early playoff exit. She led all bench players with 7.9 points a game and shot 42% from three this season, yet the spot-up shooter label no longer fits what she wants to become.Why is Sophie Cunningham not satisfied with her game?Since arriving in a 2025 trade, Cunningham has been viewed as a floor spacer who can catch and shoot at any moment, a spark off the bench when a three is needed. This season’s scoring was a slight dip from the 8.6 points and 43% from three she posted in 2025, but it was a solid return from an MCL tear.The point came up while Cunningham and Hanlen, an NBA and WNBA trainer, went through some defensive plays on the podcast. She said the level was below standard.“I’m not satisfied with where I’m at,” Cunningham said.She says she has far more to give and wants help from people like Hanlen spotting what she is missing and what she is already doing. The offseason, she said, is the time to expand, and she expects it to be a great one, with the goal of becoming a more complete player.Cunningham heads into free agency without Amber CoxIndiana’s season ended in late September with a first-round loss to the Las Vegas Aces. Indiana now has a full offseason to sort out. Amber Cox, the former general manager, made that trade. Cox is gone, so Cunningham has lost the front-office ally who made the deal, and the Fever plan to hire a new group. As an unrestricted free agent, Cunningham has no guarantee of a return for the 2027 WNBA season.The offseason has been busy away from the court. Cunningham has turned up at NASCAR events and promoted the brands she works with. She also sat down with Theo Von for his This Past Weekend show, a taping she says ran three hours or more before being trimmed to under two. Asked about the missing hours of footage, she joked it “didn’t air for a reason.” She called Von hilarious with a good heart and said the cut material was funny.Cunningham is also slated to take part in Project B, a new basketball league that tips off in January, the same month free agency opens.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Giannis, Bam Adebayo Join LeBron James, Dwyane Wade in Heat History with Rare Stat in Win vs. Cavs
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo thrived offensively as the Miami Heat secured a 133-121 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday night.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo thrived offensively as the Miami Heat secured a 133-121 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday night.

Both Antetokounmpo and Adebayo scored 37 points in the victory, becoming the second pair of Heat teammates to record at least 35 points in the same game and the first since LeBron James and Dwyane Wade accomplished the feat in 2013.

Antetokounmpo also pulled down nine rebounds and dished out two assists against Cleveland, shooting 15-of-20 from the field while connecting on one of his two attempts from behind the arc.

As for Adebayo, he shot 13-of-19 on field goals and grabbed a season-high 14 rebounds to go along with three assists.

The Heat improved to 6-6 with the victory, as they've now won six of their past eight games following an 0-4 start to the year.

Miami has turned its season around by finding much more consistency offensively, ranking No. 3 among all teams by averaging 121.3 points per game over their previous eight contests.

Antetokounmpo has experienced plenty of individual success to begin his inaugural year on the Heat, averaging 28.5 points, 12.3 rebounds and 4.9 assists per game. He's also shooting 58.3 percent from the field.

Meanwhile, Adebayo is recording 19.4 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.3 assists on a nightly basis.

The Heat will attempt to continue building momentum in their next game, a clash with the Detroit Pistons on Saturday. Tip-off is at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026: Knicks drop to last place in group play with loss to shorthanded Pacers; Spurs dominate Warriors
articles.summary: The game was nearly another Knicks comeback win.
articles.body:
The 2025-26 season was a dream for the New York Knicks, from the NBA Cup to the NBA Finals. This season is shaping up differently.

The defending Cup champions fell to 0-2 in group play on Friday with a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers, who are still playing without Tyrese Haliburton due to a left hamstring strain . That puts New York in the bottom of the East Group B standings and all but eliminates them from the in-season tournament.

No team with two losses in group play has reached the knockout rounds in the NBA Cup since its introduction in 2023.

Beyond the NBA Cup, the loss dropped the Knicks to 6-6 in the regular season, continuing a slow start for a team that brought back nearly every contributor from last year's champion.

The game was nearly another epic comeback for the Knicks, who were down by 14 late in the third quarter but had the game tied early in the fourth. The Pacers responded with a 13-2 run to reassert control and held off one last Knicks push in the final minute.

New York cut an eight-point lead to two in the final two minutes and had a chance to steal the win when an inbounds pass went wrong for the Pacers (not helped by a missed foul call by the refs), but Karl-Anthony Towns' would-be game-tying shot clanked away.

Every Pacers starter scored in double figures, with Pascal Siakam leading the team with 19 points. That plus 29 bench points was enough to counter a 33-point, 11-assist night by Jalen Brunson.

Spurs dominate Warriors after scoring first 18 points

Let's just say the second marquee game of the night did not come down to the final possession.

A clash of Western Conference contenders saw the San Antonio Spurs score the first 18 points of the game against the Golden State Warriors, who are still playing without Stephen Curry.

It honestly didn't get much better from there. The Spurs were up 63-33 at halftime and led by as much as 43 during a 123-85 blowout. That game-opening run broke a Spurs franchise record.

Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 32 points on 12-of-18 shooting, while Victor Wembanyama contributed 12 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists and 2 blocks. The win gives the Spurs a commanding lead in West Group C.

articles.title: Spurs Blow Out Warriors, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Wemby, Yaxel, Draymond, Castle, Top Players
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors started out an extended stretch without Stephen Curry with a blowout loss to the hottest team in the NBA.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors started out an extended stretch without Stephen Curry with a blowout loss to the hottest team in the NBA.

Stephon Castle racked up 32 points as the San Antonio Spurs secured a 123-85 Friday home win over a Warriors team missing Curry to an oblique abdominal tear .

The Spurs have now secured 11 straight wins to mark the team's longest victory streak since last March.

Here's a look at the top performers from Friday night's NBA Cup action as Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg struggled to step up in Curry's absence.

The Spurs opened the game with 18 unanswered points as the Warriors started out 0-for-11 from the field.

That 0-18 stretch marked the worst start by the Warriors in any game coached by Steve Kerr, per ESPN's Matt Williams (h/t ESPN's Anthony Slater ). It also marked the Spurs' largest game-opening run in the play-by-play era, according to the NBA.

The Warriors closed out the first quarter trailing by 24 points and were unable to make up any ground in the second.

The team faced a 30-point deficit by halftime, at which point Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski had combined for just two field goals.

Golden State's 33 points through two quarters marked the fewest both that the Warriors have scored and the Spurs have allowed in any first half this season, per San Antonio Spurs on SI's Matt Guzman .

The Spurs never let up down the stretch, outscoring the Warriors 60-52 in the second half to close out the blowout victory.

Castle racked up his season-high points total on 12-for-18 shooting as the Spurs outshot the Warriors 48 percent to 33 percent from the field.

San Antonio improved to 2-0 in the NBA Cup's West Group C with the win. The Spurs will now look to ride that momentum into Sunday's matchup against a Utah Jazz team on the opposite trajectory after losing 11 straight.

The Warriors will look to regroup Monday at the New Orleans Pelicans as Kerr determines what lineup will best fill in for Curry, who ESPN's Shams Charania reported the team expects could be sidelined for around a month.

articles.title: US Lifts ground stop, but passengers face second day of flight disruption
articles.summary: More than 1.5 million passengers face travel disruption as domestic and international airlines warn of knock-on delays.
articles.body:
More than 1.5 million air passengers have faced travel disruption after the United States halted departing flights nationwide for more than four hours, with airlines warning they would take days to recover.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted the ground stop at 8:15pm Eastern time on Friday (01:15 GMT on Saturday), after a telecommunications outage affected the country’s 22 regional air traffic control centres. FlightRadar24 counted more than 4,700 cancellations and 10,000 delays on Friday, with 700 flights already cancelled for Saturday.

At Los Angeles airport, passenger Nicholas Erdodi, who had travelled from New Zealand to attend a conference in Chicago, told Al Jazeera he had spent six hours at the airport after being forced off his plane.

“The challenge is you cannot ask anyone here what to do,” he said. “The lack of information is what bothers me.” He had been rebooked, but was unsure whether his next flight would go.

Others affected included sports teams in the NBA, NHL and college football.

Todd Curtis, an aviation safety expert and chief executive of AirSafe.com, told Al Jazeera that the failures appeared to be concentrated in the country’s air route traffic control centres.

“There are 21 across the United States, one in Alaska and the other 20 in the lower 48,” he said.

“These are the folks who handle the aircraft that are transiting from one part of the country to the other, and they rely on multiple handoffs between controllers.”

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it would “take us some time” to restore capacity and that “we’re going to have some makeup to do.”

He acknowledged that tens of thousands of travellers had been stranded , saying he expected operations to be back to normal for the Thanksgiving rush, which begins in less than two weeks.

Cirium, an aviation analytics firm, said about 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers were scheduled to depart US airports after 4pm Eastern time (21:00 GMT), and that at least 827 flights had been diverted by 7:05pm on Friday (00:05 am on Saturday).

The Associated Press news agency reported that the shutdown left NBA, NHL and college teams stranded, with NFL teams wondering whether they could travel in time for their games.

The Nets were among five NBA teams scheduled to fly on Friday for Saturday games. There are 14 NHL games set to play Saturday.

The San Jose Sharks were left waiting to fly to Utah, while the Florida Panthers reached St Louis before the stoppage. The Texas Longhorns had boarded their plane before it was grounded. “We are grounded and waiting to see when we can leave,” a team spokesman said.

If they have to take a bus to Baton Rouge, the trip for Saturday’s 6:30pm kickoff would take about seven hours.

Delta Air Lines said it was “safely resuming operations”, offering flexible rebooking, and warned that repositioning aircraft and crews would take time.

United Airlines said it was resuming a number of Friday night flights.

JetBlue plans to resume on Saturday morning.

Air Canada said operations would return gradually, with disruption likely on Saturday, and Aeromexico was working to resume operations.

In Mexico City, the Benito Juarez International Airport said about 70 flights scheduled for Friday could be affected.

In Canada, Toronto Pearson said flights that did not need to cross US airspace were operating as normal and that it had increased staffing to support affected passengers.

You could ask San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama to repaint the Sistine Chapel, and he would still do a masterful job.

At this point, it is clear that Wembanyama can do anything . On Friday, the Spurs hosted the Golden State Warriors at Frost Bank Arena in the NBA Cup, and the 7-foot-4 superstar showed anew why he is a cheat code.

After the Warriors turned the ball over in the third quarter, Wembanyama led the Spurs' five-man transition with nifty ball-handling. He then displayed his passing prowess with the perfect lob to Stephon Castle for the reverse slam.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While the 22-year-old center has benefited from his height and length, it is his work ethic that has shaped him into a generational talent. He has made sure to add something to his game every offseason, including the mental aspect.

Entering the game against Golden State, the two-time All-Star was averaging 30.3 points, 11.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals, and a league-leading 4.4 blocks.

Before the season, many tagged Wembanyama as the favorite to win MVP, and so far, he has lived up to the prediction. He is on a mission after losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals in June, which he did not take lightly.

As of this writing, the Spurs have a sizable lead against the Warriors in the fourth quarter. Wembanyama has 12 points, 12 rebounds, six assists, and two blocks.

articles.title: Chicago Bulls keep NBA Cup hopes alive — and snap 8-game skid. Takeaways from their OT win vs. Atlanta Hawks.
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls spent the first three weeks of the NBA season cleaving to one wishful belief: Someday, somehow, their luck had to change from behind the ar...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls spent the first three weeks of the NBA season cleaving to one wishful belief: Someday, somehow, their luck had to change from behind the arc. On Friday, that wish finally came true.

The Bulls are the worst 3-point-shooting team in the NBA. Full stop. No caveats or exceptions. Through the first 10 games of the season, the Bulls shot 28.9% from long distance.

The only team in the last two decades to shoot below 30% was the 2011-12 Charlotte Bobcats, a 7-59 squad that logged the fewest wins in history (albeit in a truncated season because of a lockout). It's too early to put the Bulls into any annals of infamy, but until Friday they had been trending toward the type of history no team wants to make. But in their 125-117 overtime win against the Atlanta Hawks on Friday, that luck turned, helping them snap an eight-game losing streak.

The Bulls went 20-for-50 (40%) on 3-pointers in their best shooting night of the season. Patrick Williams and Norman Powell each netted four 3s, while Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey offered three. Eight players made at least one 3 in the win.

Jalen Smith has been one of the only consistent shots from deep this season. So when he missed his first four attempts while his Bulls teammates watched theirs fall, he paid it no mind. The center kept shooting until his first 3 dropped in the fourth quarter.

The Bulls' hot shooting coincided with one of the worst shooting nights of the season for the Hawks, who went 8-for-40 (20%) from deep. That disparity was just enough to allow the Bulls to eke out an overtime win — and keep their hopes alive in the group stage of the NBA Cup.

"We weren't going to shoot that bad for the entire season," said Giddey, who finished with 15 points, 10 rebounds and 14 assists for his first triple-double of the season. "Guys trust the work. We trust each other. We make the extra pass. We get good looks. It's a team effort and I've said this all year — we don't have a guy that we're going to be able to just give the ball and let him go. We've got to be able to do it by committee."

In their first game without rookie Caleb Wilson — who's out four to six weeks after undergoing surgery for a fractured right hand — the Bulls found success through a simple formula: Don't give up unnecessary offensive rebounds, get to the rim when spacing opens up and feed the hot hand. On Friday, that hand belonged to Powell, who scored 33 points in his most complete game in a Bulls jersey. He scored nine of the Bulls' 15 points in overtime, taking over for isolation plays fueled by pick-and-roll sets with Isaac Okoro (15 points).

For a moment, the game seemed to be reverting into a repetitive pattern. The Bulls took an 18-point lead in the first half only to allow it to evaporate by the end of the third quarter, losing that quarter by six points despite sinking five 3s in the frame. The difference, as always, came down to ball protection. The Bulls gave the ball away eight times in the third to allow the Hawks to rack up 10 points off turnovers, a margin that overshadowed Atlanta's relatively low volume of long-range shooting.

Only two nights prior, the Bulls had a complete collapse in the third quarter, erasing a double-digit lead against the San Antonio Spurs in an eventual eighth consecutive loss . That third-quarter slump seemed to signal more of the same, but a late-game surge and Powell's overtime push fended off another collapse.

The win marked another quiet night from Buzelis. The wing made an impact by rebounding, blocking three shots and limiting his turnovers despite the smothering pressure the Hawks defense provided. But Buzelis also took only eight shots and scored only 11 points. And even with the improved spacing provided by the Bulls' elevated shooting, Buzelis couldn't carve his way to the rim with any consistency.

Coach Tiago Splitter kept Buzelis on the bench for the final six-minute stretch of the fourth quarter and opted instead to close in regulation with Patrick Williams, who finished with 13 points on 4-for-6 shooting from behind the arc. Splitter said he considered putting Buzelis back into the game for the final two minutes of regulation but kept Williams in the game to maintain the rhythm that rotation produced.

Splitter ultimately entrusted Buzelis to close the game in overtime — and the Bulls benefited when the wing sank a 3-pointer to push their lead to six with 23.5 seconds remaining.

Powell said the Bulls coaching staff didn't mention the NBA Cup in its preparation for their first group-stage game, a 125-111 loss to the Boston Celtics on Oct. 30. Against the Hawks, the Bulls took the stakes more seriously, especially with a 14-point deficit to make up after that initial loss.

The Celtics sit atop of East Group C at 2-0. With one more win, they likely will advance as the winner of the group. But the Bulls are now second in the standings at 1-1, which could position them to advance to the knockout stage of the tournament as a wild card. The wild-card spots will be decided by point differential — and with a net of minus-6, the Bulls still have ground to make up in their final two group-stage games against the Washington Wizards and Charlotte Hornets.

"If there's a prize out there, I want to get it and we want to get it," Powell said. "Just talking about the execution down the stretch — if we get a stop, we want to score. Every point matters. We're trying to make up that deficit that we had against Boston. We got to make that up to give us a chance to move on."

The only negative out of the win came in the first 30 seconds of overtime, when Smith landed awkwardly on his left hand while falling out of bounds after contesting a shot. Smith had previously strained his middle two fingers in last week's game against the Knicks in New York. He reaggravated the injury on the fall, an immediate stinger that sent him sprawling in pain and ultimately forced him to head to the locker room for the rest of the game.

Smith, who had 15 points and 12 rebounds, said that despite the immediate pain, his fingers are not broken and he believes he will play Saturday in Minnesota.

The Bulls went into Friday's game uncertain of how they would make it to Saturday's matchup in Minneapolis against the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop Friday afternoon because of an equipment outage that brought travel across the country to a halt.

The Bulls originally planned to take a charter flight out of Chicago directly after Friday's game; but the ground stop forced the delay and cancellation of hundreds of flights out of O'Hare and Midway . Splitter joked during his pregame news conference that he hoped the league wouldn't ask the team to hop on a bus for the six-hour drive to Minneapolis.

The FAA lifted the ground stop during the first half of Friday's game.

articles.title: Spurs’ Stephon Castle sets new season high in NBA Cup win over Warriors
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs made a loud statement in NBA Cup play on Friday night, and Stephon Castle was right at the center of it. The third-year guard poured i...
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs made a loud statement in NBA Cup play on Friday night , and Stephon Castle was right at the center of it. The third-year guard poured in a season-high 32 points to lead the Spurs to a 123-85 rout of the Golden State Warriors at Frost Bank Center.

Castle was nearly perfect from start to finish. He shot 12-of-18 from the field, including 5-of-8 from beyond the arc, and went 3-of-3 from the free-throw line. He also added six assists and five rebounds, finishing with a game-best plus-35 rating.

The performance easily topped his previous season high of 24 points, which he set in the season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Spurs wasted no time taking control. San Antonio opened the game on an 18-0 run, its largest to start a game in the play-by-play era, and built a 38-14 lead after the first quarter. By halftime, the lead had ballooned to 30, with Castle already sitting on 18 points and four triples.

The 2026 NBA Defensive Player of the Year did a bit of everything , posting 12 points, 12 rebounds and six assists. Keldon Johnson chipped in 18 points off the bench, while Harrison Barnes added 11.

The Warriors, meanwhile, were shorthanded without Stephen Curry, who is sidelined with a torn oblique . Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody were also out.

Golden State shot just 33.3% from the field, with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who entered averaging 21.7 points per game, going 1-of-13 for three points. LJ Cryer led the way with 20 points on six 3-pointers.

With the victory, San Antonio stretched its winning streak to 11 games and improved to 11-2 on the season. The win also gave San Antonio a leg up in the NBA Cup's Western Conference race, while Golden State dropped to 8-5 overall.

The Spurs will look to keep the streak alive when they visit the Utah Jazz on Sunday.
